Learning today, for life tomorrow
Welcome
Welcome from the Headteacher
Dear Parents, Carers and Visitors,
As Headteacher, it is my great pleasure to welcome you to Capel-le-Ferne Primary School.
We are a one-form entry school, serving children from Reception through to Year 6. At Capel-le-Ferne, we are immensely proud of our caring and inclusive school community, where every child is nurtured and valued. Our school is rooted in the core values of Independence, Confidence, Creativity, and Respect, which underpin all that we do.
Our dedicated staff are committed to ensuring that every child feels safe, supported, and inspired to achieve their very best—both academically and personally. We place great importance on mental wellbeing and social development, helping children to grow into confident, well-rounded individuals.
We offer a rich and engaging curriculum that fosters a love of learning and prepares our pupils for the next stage of their journey. Our beautiful setting and surrounding local area provide a unique backdrop for creating meaningful and memorable learning experiences that bring the curriculum to life.
We are proud of the strong partnerships we hold with parents, carers, and the wider community. We actively encourage your involvement in school life and your child’s learning. Our committed Governing Board plays a key role in both supporting and challenging the school, helping us to shape and maintain a clear strategic direction.
At Capel-le-Ferne, we are fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children, and we expect every member of staff and volunteer to share in this responsibility.
Thank you for taking the time to visit. I hope it gives you a sense of what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow. Should you require any further information, please don’t hesitate to get in touch—we would be delighted to hear from you.
Warm regards,Mr RichardsHead teacher

pageCache.text:
Tour of the School for New Parents - Sept 2026 Admissions
Starting Primary School- admissions for September 2026
Thank you for your interest in Capel-le-Ferne Primary School. Applications for transfer to primary school for reception year September 2026 will open on Friday 7th November 2025 and close on Thursday 15th January 2026.
Choosing the right school for your child is a big decision, and we understand how important it is to get it right. That’s why we’ve carefully considered how best to provide you with the information you need to decide whether Capel-le-Ferne is the right fit for your child.
One of the ways we aim to support you is by inviting you to an Open Evening, which will be held on:
During the session, I’ll talk to you about our school, our approach to education, and what your child’s learning journey at Capel-le-Ferne could look like. There will be time for questions at the end, and the focus will be on helping you make an informed choice.
Please note that these sessions do not include a school tour.
We will also be hosting a series of Open Mornings, giving you the opportunity to tour the school and see it in action during a typical day.
These sessions will take place on:
If you would like to attend one of these tours, please contact the school office to book a place. This helps us manage numbers and ensure a smooth experience for everyone visiting.
During your visit, I’ll be available for any questions you may have. You’ll also be guided by our Year 6 pupils, who will offer their honest perspective on school life here at Capel-le-Ferne.
We hope you’ll be able to join us and look forward to welcoming you to Capel-le-Ferne Primary School.
Welcome to Capel le Ferne Primary School
“Learning today for life tomorrow”
Independence, Creativity, Confidence and Respect
Welcome to Capel-le-Ferne School.
At Capel-le-Ferne we are committed to delivering a broad and balanced curriculum; to providing the best learning opportunities and learning outcomes for all children.
Our core values are to develop Independence, Creativity and Confidence underpinned by Respect for others.
We believe that to achieve the best possible education for your child, we need to foster a close relationship between home and school. Your child benefits when parents and teachers work together and there are many ways in which you can support your child at school. I hope you will regularly visit the school, becoming acquainted with your child's teachers and will be willing to join in the school's social activities.
It is our policy to keep an open dialogue with parents, ensuring that through common involvement, interest and information, problems and difficulties for the children are minimised.
Please do not hesitate to contact us if you wish to discuss any aspect of school life and how it affects your child.
Mr A Richards Headteacher
Thursday 20th November at 6.00pm
Monday 24th November at 4:00pm
Wednesday 26th November at 9:15am
Monday 1st December at 9:15am

School Clubs and Wrap Around Care
Breakfast and After School provision are provided by Caspers Nursery, which are located in the grounds of our school. For more information and details of Caspers Nursery, please see the link below-
https://www.caspernursery.co.uk/
We also offer a range of clubs after school. These clubs change termly, to offer a variety of options throughout each age group .
The school participates regularly in inter-school sports competitions.
Teachers from the Kent Music School also offer lessons in various orchestral instruments, details on request from the school office.

Information about our Governing Body
Capel-le-Ferne Primary School’s Governing Body operates under the ‘circle model’ of governance with a governing body comprising of 8 Governors. The circle model of governance means that there are only full governing body meetings, which all governors attend and there is only one committee. Responsibility for fulfilling the role of governors is shared between the committee members.
Each governor has one or more areas of responsibility and will visit the school regularly to monitor their nominated area/s and report their findings to the governing body.
As part of the schools’ leadership team, the role of the Governing Body is to ensure that standards remain high and that the school is moving forward to ensure that all pupils achieve their full potential.
